change.describe: branch `pr-67876-flat` of sentry-67876-flat against f3b740199ef0b8057c2c68a377fd3b4d42346deb (merge-base f3b7401)
change.title: pr-67876-flat
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: OAuth `state` is a constant, not a CSRF token
findings.body: `state` is `pipeline.signature`, which `src/sentry/pipeline/base.py:133` computes as an md5 of the pipeline view class names. It is the same for every user and every session, and the test hard-codes it (`9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`). The check at line 412 therefore protects against nothing. An attacker can obtain a GitHub OAuth `code` for their own account and send the victim a `/extensions/github/setup/?code=...&state=<constant>` link. The victim's pipeline then binds the attacker's login as `github_authenticated_user`. Use a per-pipeline random nonce, bound in pipeline state when the authorize redirect is issued and compared on the callback.

findings.title: KeyError when the existing Integration has no `metadata["sender"]`
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError, so the user gets a 500, if the Integration row has no `sender`. `sender` is only set from the installation webhook (`webhook.py:204`) and `build_integration` (line 376) adds it only conditionally. The sibling endpoint `installation.py:44` explicitly guards with `if "sender" not in integration.metadata`. Handle the missing key here, probably by rendering the `error()` page. Decide deliberately whether a missing sender should be allowed or rejected.

findings.title: Network and HTTP failures in the token exchange and user lookup are unhandled
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` at line 423 sits outside the `try`. `get_user_info` at line 434 calls `raise_for_status()` (`src/sentry/identity/github/provider.py:16`) and is also unguarded. A GitHub outage, a timeout, or an invalid or expired `code` that yields an HTTP error makes the setup callback return a 500 instead of the `error()` dialog used for the other failures here. Wrap both calls and return `error(...)`.

findings.title: Authorize URL is built without URL-encoding
findings.body: `redirect_uri` and `state` are interpolated directly into the query string. The redirect URI contains `://` and `/`, which is usually tolerated, but `urlencode` is the safe way to build this. The test pins the unencoded form, so update it if you change this.

findings.title: Ownership check is skipped when the Integration row doesn't exist yet
findings.body: When `Integration.objects.get` raises `DoesNotExist` (line 481), the pipeline advances without comparing the authenticated user to anything. If the installation webhook has not arrived yet, or arrives later, the OAuth step authenticates the user but never checks that they are the installer. Confirm that `build_integration` or a later step verifies the sender against `github_authenticated_user`. If it doesn't, the check only covers installations that were already webhooked.

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` no longer tests the 404 case
findings.body: The stubbed 404 for `/app/installations/...` is now never reached. The second request sends a `state` that doesn't match the pipeline signature, so the test passes on the invalid-state branch (line 412 of `integration.py`) and asserts the generic message. The original `IntegrationError("The GitHub installation could not be found.")` path in `build_integration` is left uncovered. Send the valid state so the flow reaches `build_integration`, and keep the original assertion. Add a separate test for the invalid-state case.

findings.title: No tests for the new OAuth failure branches
findings.body: The tests don't cover a failed token exchange (no `access_token`), a `get_user_info` response without `login`, a missing `sender` in metadata, or the callback arriving with no pipeline state. Add at least the missing-`access_token` and missing-`sender` cases.

contracts.action: New OAuth login step before GitHub installation step in the integration pipeline
contracts.equivalent_path: OAuth2LoginView/OAuth2CallbackView in src/sentry/identity/oauth2.py (state is a random nonce, token exchange is wrapped in try/except)
contracts.before_after: Before, the pipeline had only GitHubInstallation. Now OAuthLoginView redirects to GitHub authorize, then exchanges the code, then binds the GitHub login. The state used is the constant pipeline.signature, where the equivalent path uses a random per-flow nonce. The token exchange and user lookup are only partly guarded.
contracts.visible_effect: The user is redirected to GitHub authorize first. Failures render github-integration-failed.html through the error() helper. HTTP errors in the exchange or user lookup produce a 500.
contracts.failure_mode: safe_urlopen and get_user_info exceptions propagate as a 500. A missing sender in metadata raises KeyError at line 503.

contracts.action: GitHubInstallation compares the authenticated GitHub user to metadata.sender.login
contracts.equivalent_path: GitHubIntegrationsInstallationEndpoint.get in src/sentry/integrations/github/installation.py, which guards on `sender` presence and a 10-minute exposure window
contracts.before_after: The sibling checks that `sender` is present; the new code indexes it unconditionally and applies no time window.
contracts.visible_effect: On a mismatch the user sees the generic 'Invalid installation request.' dialog.
contracts.failure_mode: KeyError, hence a 500, if sender is absent.

contracts.action: pipeline_advancer inlines the FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR check as provider_id == "github"
contracts.before_after: The behaviour is the same. The constant had no other references in the repository.

summary: The PR adds a GitHub OAuth step that checks the installing user matches the webhook sender. Two issues matter most. The OAuth `state` is the constant `pipeline.signature`, so it gives no CSRF protection. And `integration.metadata[\"sender\"]` is read without the guard the sibling endpoint uses. The token exchange and user lookup can also raise unhandled errors. `test_installation_not_found` now exercises the invalid-state branch instead of the 404 case. The `pipeline_advancer.py` change is a harmless inline.
